text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) usually has no symptoms at all, which is why it is often called the "silent killer".

list.snippet: Most people with high blood pressure feel completely fine and do not realize their numbers are elevated.
Regular screenings from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention guidelines note that measuring your blood pressure is the only true way to know your status.

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

list.snippet: When blood pressure becomes severely elevated or spikes rapidly, subtle signs may appear.
Early-morning headaches, usually felt at the back of the head.
Nosebleeds or blood spots in the eyes.
Fatigue or shortness of breath during light physical activity.

text_blocks.snippet: Seek emergency medical care immediately if a blood pressure reading exceeds 180/120 mm Hg along with any of these critical symptoms:

list.snippet: Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Confusion, trouble speaking, or sudden weakness/numbness
Your recent blood pressure readings (if you have them)
Whether you are experiencing any specific symptoms right now
